name: Ironhand Workshop Dog Tags
description:
Stainless steel identification tags stamped with the wearer's name, blood type, augmentation registry number, and emergency medical directives. The back of each tag contains a micro-etched QR code linking to encrypted medical records. Worn on a ball chain around the neck.

Originating from military tradition but now standard among augmented workers, runners, and anyone who operates in environments where they might end up unconscious and in need of medical treatment from someone who doesn't know their history. The tags communicate: I might not be able to speak for myself, so this will speak for me.
functionality: Emergency identification, medical data access, augmentation registry
what_it_says: You live a life where someone might need to identify your body, and you've made that easier for them.
story_hooks: A set of dog tags recovered from a body list an augmentation registry number that is still active — the augmentations were removed and installed in someone else before the body was dumped.

physical_description.visual_profile: A pair of small rectangular stainless steel tags suspended on a worn ball chain around the neck. The tags catch light with a dull metallic gleam, hanging at mid-chest. The overall impression is utilitarian, honest, and subtly defiant—a public declaration of preparedness and augmentation status.
physical_description.fit: Loose around the neck on adjustable ball chain; tags rest naturally at chest level. Not form-fitting; designed to be visible and accessible.
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed stainless steel tags; surgical-grade ball chain in nickel or titanium alloy
physical_description.texture: Smooth brushed metal face with slight grip texture from micro-etching on reverse; chain has fine segmented links with subtle wear patina
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte silver-gray steel with darker etched text and QR code on reverse. Chain develops a soft bronze patina over time from body heat and wear.
physical_description.closures: Ball chain held together by simple split ring or crimp connector; no clasp—meant to be permanent or semi-permanent
distinctive_features: Front face stamped with name, blood type, augmentation registry number
Micro-etched QR code on reverse linking to encrypted medical database
Slight dents or scratches from impact exposure—common in working conditions
Faint oxidation marks from skin contact and sweat exposure
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional; standard among augmented workers and street operatives. Accessible pricing (50-200 Φ) but signals someone with integrated tech and street-smart preparedness.
physical_description.tier_indicator_explanation: Not a luxury item, but essential infrastructure for anyone with augmentations or living in high-risk environments. Wearing them signals you're augmented, medically complex, and operating in spaces where corpo hospitals might not have your records.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by augmented workers, military veterans, runners, street medics, anyone with non-standard biology or combat implants. Signals self-awareness about mortality and the need for others to understand your body without you speaking. A quiet cry for help before you need it.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn and broken-in. Tags show minor dents from impacts, chain develops a patina, edges lose their factory sharpness. The weathered look is intentional and expected—pristine tags suggest someone who hasn't needed them yet.
